title: The subfield with $q^n$ elements of an algebraic closure of $\mathbf F_q$

source.place: node def-weil-finite-field-fiber, order 411: 'For every integer $n\geq1$, let $\mathbf F_{q^n}\subset k$ be the unique subfield with $q^n$ elements' (existence and uniqueness asserted without argument; the $k_0$-algebra structure of $\mathbf F_{q^n}$, needed for $\operatorname{Hom}_{k_0}(\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf F_{q^n},Y_0)$, is not mentioned). No document in literature/ proves it: Stacks Tag 09HY (Fields, Section 9.14) only shows that a finite field has $p^f$ elements and a cyclic unit group; the standard reference is Lang, Algebra, Ch. V, §5, Theorem 5.1 (not obtained)

mathlib_searches.results: only the prime subfield: Subfield.card_bot : Nat.card (⊥ : Subfield F) = p (Basic.lean:722), Subfield.roots_X_pow_char_sub_X_bot (:734), Subfield.mem_bot_iff_pow_eq_self : x ∈ (⊥ : Subfield F) ↔ x ^ p = x (:748); GaloisField p n is an abstract splitting field with p ^ n elements (GaloisField.lean:69, :130), not a subfield of a given algebraically closed field; FiniteField.Extension k p n (Extension.lean) is a non-canonically chosen extension of degree n of a finite field k
mathlib_searches.verdict: no match: clause (3) for a = 1 (the prime subfield is the set of roots of X^p - X and has p elements) is Subfield.mem_bot_iff_pow_eq_self with Subfield.card_bot; nothing states that the roots of X^{q^n} - X in an algebraically closed field of characteristic p form the unique subfield with q^n elements
